*adjusts environmental suit nervously, pulling up diagnostic displays*

Keelah, this code... it's like someone vented the thermal regulators and expected the drive core not to melt. Let me walk you through what I found.

## Critical Issues

**SQL Injection (Lines 97, 107-109, 125, 147-149, 179-181, 192-194)**
The queries use string concatenation with user input. An attacker could execute `?id=1; DROP TABLE orders--` and destroy everything. This is critical - use parameterized queries everywhere.

**Storing Credit Cards in Plain Text (Lines 30, 78, 192)**
You're storing full credit card numbers in the database unencrypted. This violates PCI-DSS and could result in massive fines. Never store card numbers - use tokenization through your payment processor.

## High Severity

**No Error Handling on HTTP Calls (Lines 52-53, 59-63, 68-74, 128-129, 136-140)**
You're ignoring errors from `http.Get` and `http.Post`. If inventory check fails silently, you'll charge customers for items you can't ship.

**Race Condition on Cache Access (Lines 86, 113, 142)**
You use `cacheMutex` but never actually lock it. Line 86 writes to the cache without synchronization. Multiple goroutines will corrupt the map.

**Goroutine Variable Capture Bug (Lines 136-140)**
The goroutine captures `productID` and `quantity` by reference. By the time it executes, the loop has moved on. Every release call will use the last item's values.

## Medium Severity

**No Response Body Closure (Lines 52, 63, 102)**
You never call `resp.Body.Close()`. This leaks connections and will eventually exhaust file descriptors.

**Payment Before Atomic Inventory Reserve (Lines 59-74)**
You charge the customer, then fire-and-forget inventory reservations. If reservation fails, customer is charged for nothing. This needs to be transactional.

**No Authorization Checks (Entire file)**
Anyone can cancel any order, view any user's orders, process refunds. No authentication or ownership verification.

**Float64 for Money (Lines 27, 49)**
Floating point arithmetic causes rounding errors. Use integer cents or a decimal library.

## Low Severity

**Credit Card in JSON Response (Line 88)**
Even with `omitempty`, the order struct still contains the card and gets cached. Sanitize before responding.

**Card Masking Panic (Line 200)**
If `creditCard` is empty or less than 4 characters, this panics. Add bounds checking.

**No Request Timeout (Lines 52, 63, etc.)**
HTTP calls with no timeout can hang forever under load.

---

*sighs, leaning back from the terminal*

I can fix this. Just give me a minute with the core. But whoever wrote this needs to understand - we're not just shuffling data here. Real money, real people. The implementation needs to be as resilient as the Migrant Fleet, not as fragile as a quarian's immune system outside their suit.
